text.p: A hard-line labor group Thursday walked off from the board of ArgentinaPs main union federation CGT, denouncing its plans to introduce more flexibile working conditions.

The Argentine Workers Movement (MTA) said it was not consulted by the CGT on talks it was holding with government officials on the government's plans to accept smaller severance payments and other aspects of a plan popularly known as "labor flexibilization."
"We will not give our blessing to the labor flexibilization agreement this ladership is promoting," MTA leader Juan Manuel Palacios told reporters.
President Carlos Menem argues that reforms would help combat current unemployment of more than 17 percent.

The reforms proposed by the president include swapping redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance and allowing workers to make salary and working condition deals directly with employers with no centralized union intervention.
He is also pushing for the complete deregulation of the union-controlled private health system.

Unions, fearing that workers would lose rights and that they would lose influence and income, have fought back with strikes and are backed by the courts, who object to Menem's attempts to reform by decree rather than through Congress.
